title: Recovery of the First Bit String
statement: Let $x,U,t,a,j,p$ be finite bit strings, and let $\langle u,v\rangle$ denote the encoding formed by doubling each bit of $u$, appending the separator $01$, and then appending $v$. If $\pi_1$ is the total first projection that returns the first component of a pair encoding and returns the empty string otherwise, then applying $\pi_1$ twice to $\langle\langle x,U\rangle,\langle\langle t,a\rangle,\langle j,p\rangle\rangle$ gives $x$.
